Antimonium Arsenicicum.



Arseniate of Antimony. (Sb 2  O 3 )
        As O 5  + 3 p.c. Trituration.



Clinical. ─   Catarrhal pneumonia. Emphysema.
        Ophthalmia. Pericarditis. Phthisis. Pleurisy. Pneumonia. Sciatica.



Characteristics. ─     Antim.
        ars  . is said to affect preferably upper left lung. Emphysema where the dyspnœa
        is excessive. Haarer is the chief authority for this drug. Mattes, who used it after him,
        says it is equally effective in right-side cases in old pneumonias and catarrhal pneumonias
        in children; in old pleuritic effusions, and in pericardial exudations. The cough is   <   by eating, and on lying down. Wandering pains in sciatic
        nerves. It has caused inflammation of the eyes and œdema of the face.



Relations. ─     Compare:
        Other antimony salts, Ars., Aur., Laches., Puls. (wandering pains), Sul.
